keep.quote: in mice the spaces between brain cells open up by about sixty per cent during sleep and waste washes out faster (c12), so sleep is when your brain takes the trash out, and yours hasn't in a month; about a hundred years ago, in a test on two people, they forgot less after sleeping than after the same hours awake (c13), and in rats the day's activity replays during sleep, faster than real time (c14): your brain files your day at night, on fast forward, and nothing has been filed.
